claims.statement: movie-mcp, web-api-mcp and spreadsheet-mcp are stateless streamable-HTTP MCP servers built on the MCP Python SDK 2.x (`MCPServer`, `mcp>=2,<3`) that the Agent Gateway calls as tools; each is scoped to one capability and one trust boundary across three jointly-moving dimensions — the tools it registers, the identity it carries, and the network it can reach.

movie-mcp carries the caller's downscoped `aud=mc-service` JWT out-of-band as the request's `Authorization: Bearer` header (never an LLM-visible tool argument); a pure-ASGI middleware — deliberately not Starlette's `BaseHTTPMiddleware`, whose separate task would break ContextVar propagation — binds it into a request-scoped ContextVar, resets it after the request, and fails closed with `PermissionError` when no token is present rather than issuing an unauthenticated mc-service call.

movie-mcp adds no domain logic: it registers nine tools (reads `list_collections`, `get_collection`, `list_movies`, `count_movies`, `get_movie_metadata`; writes `create_collection`, `add_movie`, `update_movie`, `delete_movie` carrying an `idempotencyKey` and executing only on the approved-resume path), passes mc-service's shapes through verbatim, and re-raises mc-service 4xx/5xx as an MCP tool error carrying a stable `mc-service-status:<code>` sentinel — with a fixed input-validation `detail` appended only for 400/422 — so the gateway can classify a 409 as `skipped_duplicate` without parsing mc-service's body.

The `mc-service-status:<code>` sentinel only survives because `McServiceToolError` subclasses the SDK's `ToolError`: on MCP SDK 2.x an exception raised deliberately by a tool keeps its message, while anything else is treated as a crash and its text is withheld from the model, so a plain exception base silently dropped the sentinel and degraded every downstream status classification.

web-api-mcp authenticates to TMDB with the requesting user's own v3 key, forwarded per request as the `X-TMDB-Key` header; that header is the sole source of the key (no shared env/Vault fallback by design), a call arriving without one raises a clear configuration error instead of issuing an unauthenticated request, and a pure-ASGI middleware binds and resets the value per request so it never leaks across calls.

Because TMDB v3 authenticates with an `api_key` query parameter, the user's key is embedded in every request URL; web-api-mcp's `build_app()` therefore raises `httpx`/`httpcore` logging to WARNING (dropping the per-request `HTTP Request: GET <url>` line) and attaches a redacting filter to the root logger and its handlers — the one place among the three servers that configures logging at all, and it exists to suppress credential-bearing output rather than to add application logging.

web-api-mcp's network footprint enforces its outbound-only role: it is deliberately NOT attached to `backend-network` (no internal-service access) and instead sits on the isolated `movie-assistant-mcp-network` that only the Agent Gateway bridges to the backend, with no published host port.
movie-mcp attaches to `backend-network` only, so it can reach mc-service by Docker service DNS, and publishes no host port — the Agent Gateway is its sole caller.

spreadsheet-mcp reaches no backend domain service: it registers `parse_spreadsheet`, `build_workbook`, `stash_parsed` and `fetch_parsed`, all invoked from pure code by the import/export nodes by opaque handle (never an LLM-chosen path or content), and it is token-free — the gateway's server config sets `needs_token=False` and its acquire-token seam is a no-op.

spreadsheet-mcp's transient store semantics differ per namespace: `import:file:<handle>` uploads are single-use (the key is deleted after a successful read so a handle cannot be replayed), `export:file:<handle>` plus `export:name:<handle>` downloads carry a 15-minute TTL, and `import:parsed:<handle>` parsed-import contexts carry a 60-minute TTL that is refreshed on every read and never consumed so a multi-turn import cannot expire mid-session.

spreadsheet-mcp's `stash_parsed`/`fetch_parsed` exist so a guided import checkpoints only a small opaque handle instead of re-serializing the whole parsed dataset into LangGraph state on every clarification turn — the checkpoint-bloat cause of an import that timed out — and the gateway's deny-by-default allowlists reflect the split: `import_collection` may call `parse_spreadsheet`, `stash_parsed` and `fetch_parsed`, while `export_collection` may call `build_workbook`.

All three servers disable DNS-rebinding host validation by passing `TransportSecuritySettings(enable_dns_rebinding_protection=False)` explicitly to `streamable_http_app()` (a parameter of `streamable_http_app()` on SDK 2.x, not an `MCPServer()` constructor kwarg), because the SDK's auto-enabled `allowed_hosts` would otherwise 421-reject a request addressed to a Docker service name; a bare `streamable_http_app()` silently re-enables the protection. The SDK's `host` parameter is deliberately not passed — it is not a bind address (the bind stays at each server's `*_MCP_HOST`/`*_MCP_PORT` uvicorn entrypoint) but only the trigger for the auto-enable branch that an explicit `transport_security` already skips.

Every `@mcp.tool()`-decorated function in all three servers declares a precise return annotation (`dict[str, Any]` / `list[dict[str, Any]]`) rather than a bare `dict`, bare `list`, `Any`, or none, because on MCP SDK 2.x a bare `dict` annotation produces `structured_content: None` — the assistant silently receives text only, with no test failing and no error logged.

Each server's `configure_otel()` wires an OTLP exporter only when `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` is set (a no-op otherwise), and each `tool_span` wraps a tool body in a span named `tool.<name>` carrying the tool name only — never arguments, headers, handles, or credentials — with both `record_exception=False` and `set_status_on_exception=False` so an upstream exception, whose stringification can include a credential-bearing request URL, never reaches the exported trace.

The SC-004 token-leak scan is a static AST pass over `agents/movie-assistant/src`, `mcp-servers/movie-mcp/src` and `mcp-servers/web-api-mcp/src` that flags any `logging`/`print` call emitting a token-named variable; spreadsheet-mcp's source is not among the scan roots because it carries no user credential, not because it is exempt from the rule.

web-api-mcp's `get_movie_details` appends `release_dates` to the TMDB request it already makes and derives the film's real US certification: only US blocks are considered, the first non-empty certification wins (TMDB routinely publishes an empty entry ahead of a real one), and the value is accepted only when it is in `{G, PG, PG-13, R, NC-17, NR, Unrated}`; anything else yields `null` rather than the positive claim `"NR"`, and there is no rename from `PG-13` to `PG13` because mc-service's wire form is hyphenated.

spreadsheet-mcp's builder and parser are a matched pair around one formula-injection hardening rule: the builder escapes a cell whose text begins with `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab or CR by prefixing an apostrophe, and the parser strips exactly that guard, so an export→import round trip is symmetric while a legitimate leading apostrophe is preserved.

spreadsheet-mcp's store client is a lazily created process-shared instance rather than one built per tool call, because building a fresh `redis.from_url` client and its connection pool on every call leaks pools and sockets over the long-lived server process; the integration suite works around this by resetting the shared client per test, since a `redis.asyncio` client binds to the event loop that created it.

All three server images build from the repository root as context (`docker build -f mcp-servers/<server>/Dockerfile .`) on a digest-pinned `python:3.14-slim` base, sync the pinned lockfile with `uv sync --frozen --no-dev`, and run as a non-root `app` user with the virtualenv and source mounted read-only, entering via `python -m src.server`.

Each server exposes the Nx targets `test` (unit), `test:integration`, `lint` (ruff + mypy), `build` (Docker image tagged `<server>:latest`) and `lock`, and all three integration suites run together in the app-ci job with `MCM_REQUIRE_LIVE_STACK=1` turning an unexpected skip into a failure, because a suite that skips when its dependency is absent reports green and gives false confidence — how two spreadsheet-mcp tests sat broken and unexecuted for weeks.

`scripts/agent-stack.mjs` builds all three MCP images plus the gateway and publishes loopback-only host ports for the MCP servers (8765 web-api, 8766 movie, 8767 spreadsheet) purely so host-side callers such as `nx test:integration movie-assistant` can reach the containerized servers; inside the stack the gateway reaches them by Docker DNS and needs none of those ports.

spreadsheet-mcp is attached to both `backend-network` (so the Agent Gateway, its sole caller, can reach it) and `mcm-bff-network` (so it can reach the transient store Redis that lives on the BFF network), and it makes no backend domain-service calls — it has no mc-service client and no `MC_SERVICE_URL`.

The gateway attaches the two credential channels independently through a request hook rather than default client headers: the downscoped bearer rides `Authorization` only on movie-server calls and the per-run TMDB key rides `X-TMDB-Key` only on the external-API server call, each omitted when its context variable is unset, so a movie-mcp call never carries a TMDB key and a web-api-mcp call never carries a bearer token.
